meta.title: Case study · DSimoles — Ginés López Montalbán
meta.description: DSimoles exposes two things: a framework for defining and documenting design systems (DSBook) and the design system of the iMoles ecosystem for medical applications with WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility.

foot.disclaimer: DSimoles is under construction: token and component values are proposals pending review by its owner.

hero.title: DSimoles: a framework for design systems and the iMoles ecosystem DS
hero.sub: Two things are exposed here at once: DSBook, a reusable framework to define, document and track a design system, and DSimoles, the design system of the iMoles ecosystem for medical applications with WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility, built with that framework.
hero.lead: The starting point is the prototype from the iMoles project review: it provides the products, requirements and components the design system has to cover. The framework opens right here, in the browser, with all its content.

facts.v: Design and architecture of the system, and of the method to build it

deliverables.heading: What is exposed
deliverables.intro: The DSimoles repository holds two layers that can be read separately: the method, and the system obtained by applying it.

cards.label: Framework
cards.title: DSBook
cards.text: A workspace to define, document and track a design system, designed to be reused in other projects.
points: Definition guide with one subsection per decision and its acceptance criteria.
Tracking matrix with statuses (Ready, In process, Pending, Not applicable) and a recorded review.
Static HTML documentation container, with no build step or external services.
Workflow between Claude Design, Claude Code and Git, with protection against losing work.

cards.label: Design system
cards.title: DSimoles for the iMoles ecosystem
cards.text: The design system for the medical applications of the iMoles ecosystem, defined with the framework.
points: Primitive and semantic tokens, with themes.
Base components and patterns, plus iMoles-specific product components (for example the risk badge, the capture row or the analysis summary).
WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility as a requirement, not an extra.
Governance: how something in the system is added, changed or deprecated.

start.heading: Starting point
start.callout: The initial starting point is the prototype from the iMoles project review.
paragraphs: That navigable prototype of the dermatological pre-diagnosis app fixes the products, flows and requirements the design system has to serve. DSimoles does not start from a generic component catalogue: it starts from what that proposal needs and generalises it where it makes sense.
That is why base and iMoles-specific components live side by side in the system, and why the guide content (users, products, requirements) is written from that case.

method.heading: How it works
method.intro: The repository is the source of truth. Design and implementation are split between two tools and a person who validates.

steps.def: It is the only source of truth for the system.
Reads the repository, designs and builds the page for each section.
Brings the changes in, integrates them locally and runs the data-contract and test checks.
The responsible person reviews locally; nothing is pushed without their approval.
Each integration is logged in the changelog and Claude Design is told to continue from the new base.

state.heading: Status
paragraphs: Of the 175 subsections in the guide, 25 are Ready with a recorded review, 46 are in process, 1 is pending and 103 are marked not applicable, each with an explicit reason.
An existing page does not imply Ready: that status requires a recorded review, not an automatic certification.
state.note: Figures correspond to project version 0.29.0 (2026-10-15) and change with each integration.
